speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development how can the Ministry urgently implement and communicate a nationwide action plan to help families in need to apply for the appointment of Deputies for family members who have lost their mental capacity due to accidents, dementia or other disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But before I explain more about deputyship, let me say that a better option would be for Singaporeans to plan ahead and make an LPA.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: One key advantage of making an LPA is that the individual is able to choose his proxy decision-maker and discuss the LPA with his family so that his wishes are made known.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, the key thing is, the better option really is for Singaporeans to plan ahead and make the LPA ahead of time.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In order to encourage Singaporeans to do so, can I ask the Members of this House to please encourage your residents to do so?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We hope that many, many more Singaporeans will take advantage of the fee waiver to pre-plan.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Broadly, allow me to share some initiatives which my Ministry is undertaking to streamline the deputyship process further.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We are also discussing with the Courts regarding how deputyship applications may be made more accessible to families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Last year, we partnered the Family Justice Courts and the Movement for the Intellectually Disabled in Singapore (MINDS) on a pilot project to simplify the deputyship application process for parents of MINDS students.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In working on the MINDS project, we realised the need to have a better, more standardised mental capacity assessment form which could be submitted to the Courts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Hence, we have organised an inter-agency committee to develop a mental capacity assessment form for Page: 18 deputyship which covers key domain areas of capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Special Education schools and doctors could, in future, use the form for their students and patients respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Families in financial difficulty can seek legal assistance from the Legal Aid Bureau under the Ministry of Law to file the deputyship application.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Applicants will have to go through a means test and merits test to qualify for legal aid.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: First, how can we increase the number of Singaporeans to complete the LPA?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: More of them instead of remaining at the current level, which is already an encouragement, but grossly still insufficient.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The second question is: there is still much concern and lack of awareness amongst the families where the members are older than 21 and presumed to be lacking in mental capacity.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many of them are affected and could not proceed in quite a number of life decisions, for example, in healthcare, property and financial matters because they have not had their deputies to act on their behalf.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, for this group, what more can be done for them, because they are currently in a limbo?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How can the state help this group of persons?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As mentioned earlier, the numbers have been increasing but I would agree that the numbers are nowhere near what we would like them to be, short of compelling and making it compulsory.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The last mile really needs to be taken by the individual.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, I do ask for Members' support to encourage their residents to do so.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are doing as much as we can to raise awareness and that is something that we will keep on doing.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With regard to the second question, I have highlighted some of the various processes available right now to assist the individuals.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Where possible, decisions to take up the LPA should be done as early as possible so that individuals can pre-plan.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For those who do have some of these incapacities already and are concerned about what they can do, then some of the steps highlighted earlier should be taken.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But again, the main thing is to help raise awareness amongst all the various individuals concerned, so that they can take the necessary steps.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Can the Ministry consider amending the law to allow parents of children without mental capacity to make an LPA on their behalf?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Currently, the children already cannot make an LPA, so can the parents do so on their behalf so that we can dispense with the need to apply for an order under the Mental Capacity Act?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For instance, relatives could be abusive and could also have debilitating illnesses that impair their own mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is important for a judicial body like the Family Justice Courts to evaluate and make the decisions accordingly.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Can I know when the procedure simplification would take effect?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: From what we understand now, the application process remains very complex because judges are understandably, as the Minister noted also, very concerned about the applications.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: The second question is in relation to the forms.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: While we are trying to encourage people to apply and sign the LPA, are there ways to simplify the forms so that it is actually easier for them?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: A very simple example will be that currently, the form requires a legal seal to be affixed and anyone filling up the form at home would not have access to all those little red stickers.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: So, these are little oddities that should not even be present.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Would the Ministry consider revising the form to make it more user-friendly?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are taking on board feedback from the public and from concerned individuals.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I am not sure whether the Member has surfaced some of these particular pieces of feedback, but the idea is to continually improve and to make it as easy as possible while at the same time making sure that it is sufficiently rigorous.
